title: Chapter 69 — The Funeral
paragraphs: "Haul in the chains! Let the carcass go astern!"

The vast tackles have now done their work. The peeled white body of the beheaded whale gleams like a marble tomb, though changed in color, it has not visibly lost anything in bulk. It is still colossal. Slowly it floats farther and farther away, the water around it torn and splashed by the insatiable sharks, and the air above harassed by rapacious birds, whose beaks are like so many insulting daggers in the whale's body. The vast white headless phantom floats farther from the ship, and every step that it so floats, what seem square roods of sharks and cubic yards of birds augment the monstrous funeral procession.

What a most sorrowful and mocking funeral! The sea-vultures all in pious mourning, the air-sharks all punctiliously dressed in black or speckled. In life, few of them would have helped the whale, I think, if he had needed it. But upon the banquet of his funeral, they most devoutly descend. Horrible vultureism of earth! From which not even the mightiest whale is free.

Nor is this the end. Desecrated as the body is, a vengeful ghost survives and hovers over it to scare. Spotted by some timid warship or blundering discovery-vessel from afar — when the distance obscures the swarming birds but still shows the white mass floating in the sun, and the white spray heaving high against it — straightaway the whale's ghost becomes a terrifying reef. On the charts, the spot is marked with an "S" for shoal, and a new hazard is added to the navigator's dangers.
Thus, while in life the great whale's body may have been a real terror to his enemies, in his death his ghost becomes a powerless panic to a world.
Are you a believer in ghosts, my friend? There are other ghosts than the Cock-Lane one, and far deeper men than Doctor Johnson who believe in them.
